messages:
Anita: perf CI flagged a regression after the kv prefetch/scheduler tweak landed. nightly tokens/sec down ~12%. report: https://ci.internal/reports/1937654321

Diego: confirming on canary, p95/p99 increased, queue depth spikes, overall throughput drop.

Maya: can you paste the nightly numbers? quick before/after helps triage.

Anita: snapshot from the job:
```
baseline: tokens/sec=152k, p99=36ms, mean_batch_size=12.1
after (commit 9b2f4c): tokens/sec=133k, p99=59ms, mean_batch_size=7.9
distribution: spike in 1-5 token batches
```

Diego: did a local bisect, points at PR #4527 (kv prefetch + scheduling). That PR increased prefetch_threshold_ms and nudged batch_window_ms.

Lu: widening batch_window should have increased batching. odd that mean batch size dropped.

Anita: profiler shows skewed queueing: some inflight requests are drained early by a backfill path, leaving many tiny batches. prefetch backfill appears to race window expiry.

Diego: flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/flame/1937654321 shows hot in kv_prefetch::backfill -> schedule_batch and a lot of small memcpy ops.

Lu: runtime switches to fallback kernel when batch_size < 8; that path does extra staging copies. profiler shows ~10-13% time in memcpy and kernel_fallback_dispatch post-change.

Maya: so causal chain: prefetch timing change -> more small early batches -> fallback kernel + memcpy overhead -> tokens/sec drop.

Anita: agreed. immediate plan: 1) revert the prefetch timing on canary, 2) add unit/bench test for batch-shape distribution, 3) CI perf gate for median batch size and kernel-selection counters.

Diego: reverted on canary; short run shows tokens/sec improved to ~142k, p99 down to ~46ms (partial recovery). still slightly below baseline.

ops-bot: deploy canary revert completed to eng-runtime-canary at 1937654330 :white_check_mark:

Lu: there's still a residual gap. I'll add kernel-selection counters (primary vs fallback) to metrics and ship to canary.

Anita: I'll add a temporary runtime guard: if mean_batch_size < 9 then prefer primary kernel to avoid memcopy fallback while we stabilize.

Maya: +1. Also change prefetch backfill to yield if applying it would create batches smaller than min_batch_size. Add tests:
- synthetic mixed short/long workloads reproducer
- assert kernel-selection counts match baseline
- assert no rapid oscillation between schedule/backfill paths

Diego: added JIRA RED-9876 and attached bisect outputs and perf snapshots.

Anita: holding the main rollout until canary metrics look normal. @eng-runtime stand by. :eyes:

ops-bot: rollout flag set: HOLD (reason: perf-regression 1937654321) by Anita at 1937654340

Lu: local reproduce notes:
```
./bench --mix "short:0.65,long:0.35" --rate 600
expected mean_batch_size ~12
observed mean_batch_size ~8 after 9b2f4c
```

Diego: confirm bisect commit 9b2f4c -> PR #4527. attaching artifacts to RED-9876.

Anita: next steps: Diego run longer canary (1h) with revert, Lu push kernel metrics, Maya add tests & CI perf check, Anita keep rollout blocked until metrics are back to baseline. ping here with progress or quick mitigations.

Diego: I'll post the 1h canary numbers when done.

Maya: I'll draft the CI perf check patch (median batch size + kernel fallback rate) and try to land it in the perf CI pipeline tomorrow.

Anita: thanks all.
